dossier.public_summary: The 0.80-day dip repeats every starspot spin and the star shows strong brightness swings at that same period, with a large out-of-eclipse signal. The 1.2-hour dip is much longer than expected for this M-dwarf and fits best as rotation/spots, not a 1.9 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Dip period is essentially exactly the spot rotation period with large-amplitude pulsations/spots phase curve amplitude_ppm=4418 ratio_to_depth=1.082 chi2=126.9 dof=9, so large phase-curve swing at the same period. favours stellar variability over planet.
Very long duration for the M-dwarf density, fit_log_density_ratio=-2.233, combined with high phase-curve and rotation match makes a planet less likely than a spotted binary/rotation harmonic.
